events.title: Archbishop Ussher's date for the Creation
events.description: In his chronology of 1650, Archbishop James Ussher calculated from biblical genealogies that the world was created on the evening before Sunday 23 October 4004 BCE. The date was printed in many English Bibles for two centuries.

events.title: Brutus takes his own life after defeat at Philippi
events.description: Defeated by Mark Antony and Octavian in the second engagement at Philippi in Macedonia, Marcus Junius Brutus, a leader of Julius Caesar's assassins, took his own life. The triumvirs' victory ended the Liberators' civil war and the republican cause.

events.title: A synod at Palma refuses to judge Pope Symmachus
events.description: Urged by the Ostrogothic king Theodoric to settle the matter, the bishops met at Palma and declared they could not judge Pope Symmachus, successor of Peter the Apostle, leaving it to God. The resolutions were signed by 76 bishops.

events.title: Yusuf ibn Tashfin's Almoravids defeat Alfonso VI at Sagrajas
events.description: Near Badajoz, the Almoravid army of Yusuf ibn Tashfin, called in by the taifa rulers of al-Andalus, shattered the forces of King Alfonso VI of Castile. The victory preserved Muslim control of southern Spain under Almoravid influence.

events.title: Valdemar I defeats Sweyn III at Grathe Heath
events.description: Near Viborg in Jutland, Valdemar I defeated his rival for the Danish throne, Sweyn III, who was killed while fleeing. The battle ended the Danish civil wars, and Valdemar became sole king.

events.title: Scotland and France seal the first treaty of the Auld Alliance
events.description: A treaty between John Balliol of Scotland and Philip IV of France, signed in Paris, formed the Auld Alliance against England. Renewed by most later Scottish kings, it drew Scotland into repeated wars with England and effectively ended in 1560.

events.title: Royalists and Parliamentarians clash at Edgehill
events.description: Charles I's army fought Parliament's forces under the Earl of Essex at Edgehill in Warwickshire, the first pitched battle of the English Civil War. The indecisive result made clear the war would be long.

events.title: The Hungarian Revolution begins in Budapest
events.description: A student demonstration in Budapest grew into a national uprising against the communist government and Soviet control. Soviet forces crushed it in November, leaving some 2,500 Hungarians dead and 200,000 in exile.

events.title: Truck bombs kill 241 US and 58 French troops in Beirut
events.description: Suicide bombers drove explosive-laden trucks into the US Marine barracks and a French paratroop building in Beirut. The attacks led to the withdrawal of the multinational peacekeeping force from Lebanon.
